added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(C_0\) be a set of observed root vertices of a finite labeled DAG \(G\), let \(X\) and \(Y\) be disjoint vertex sets outside \(C_0\), and let \(L_{C_0}\) be maximal-regular with respect to \(G\) in the sense of Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash. In their positive-observed-law structural-equation-model class, \(P_{\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)\) is identifiable from \((G,L_{C_0})\) if and only if it is identifiable from every context DAG
\[
G_c=\bigl((V\setminus C_0)\cup U,\, (E(G)\cap(((V\setminus C_0)\cup U)\times((V\setminus C_0)\cup U)))\setminus L_{C_0}(c)\bigr),
\qquad c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}.
\]
When every context query is identified by an observed-law formula \(F_c\), their Algorithm 1 returns
\[
\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}}P(C_0=c)F_c\!\left(P(V\setminus C_0\mid C_0=c)\right).
\]

source.locator: Definitions 2, 3, and 6, Theorem 1, and Algorithm 1, PMLR 151, pages 11240--11243

attestation.note: Checked against the primary PMLR PDF at the stated definitions, theorem, and algorithm; the node records the if-and-only-if context-graph criterion and the successful formula assembled by Algorithm 1. A stable primary-source URL is supplied in lieu of a long verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((G,L_{C_0},X,Y,\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\) be a maximal-regular observed-root input of Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash, with the used hypotheses written explicitly as follows: \(C_0\subseteq V\) consists of observed roots; \(X,Y\subseteq V\setminus C_0\) are disjoint; \(L_{C_0}(c)\) is the label set at \(c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}\); and, for every labeled edge \(a\to i\), the set \(C_i=\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\cap C_0\) is nonempty and
\[
c|_{C_i}=c'|_{C_i}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl(a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c)\Longleftrightarrow a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c')\bigr).
\]
Compile a label \(a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c)\) into the whole-row CSI equating the complete conditional vectors of child \(i\) across values of parent \(a\), activated at \(C_i=c_i\), where \(c_i=c|_{C_i}\). Denote the compiled list by \(\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\). Put \(\mathbf d=(|\mathcal X_j|:j\in V\cup U)\). Let \(\Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G)\) be this note's fixed-finite-state, latent-root, two-child-latent, independent-latent, strictly primitive-positive CPT class before imposing CSI, and let \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0})\) denote the published compatible labeled-DAG class in the same stochastic-CPT representation. Then
\[
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}\!\left(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\right)
=
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0})
\cap \Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G).
\]
For every \(c\), the complete active compiled trace \(t_c\) has
\[
H_{k(c),t_c}[(V\setminus C_0)\cup U]=G_c,
\]
where \(k(c)\) is the activation-partition cell containing context \(c\); and the compiled quotient \(\mathcal R_i\) is exactly the connected row-equality quotient generated by the labels of child \(i\). If every \(G_c\) identifies the context query with formula \(F_c\), the compiled SUCCESS derivations assemble the same formula as the published algorithm,
\[
E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}}P(C_0=c)
F_c\!\left(P(V\setminus C_0\mid C_0=c)\right)
=P_{\mathbf x}(\mathbf y),
\]
and every displayed conditioning divisor is positive. This transfers the published identification implication to the intersection above. It does not assert that failure in one \(G_c\) implies nonidentification on the narrower fixed-cardinality positive class. Finally, \(\mathsf E_5\) is admitted by this note's input syntax but not by the observed-root-control syntax: its activation variable \(X\) is observed and satisfies \(U\to X\), so the activation \(X=0\) is endogenous.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(E(G)\) for the edge set of \(G\) and
\[
\mathcal X_A:=\prod_{j\in A}\mathcal X_j
\]
for the finite state space of a vertex set \(A\). We first check that the compilation is well defined. For a child \(i\), put
\[
C_i:=\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\cap C_0.
\]
The stated regularity hypothesis says that \(C_i\neq\varnothing\) whenever an edge into \(i\) is labeled. The stated maximality hypothesis says that if \(c,c'\in\mathcal X_{C_0}\) have \(c|_{C_i}=c'|_{C_i}\), then
\[
a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c').
\]
Consequently membership of \(a\to i\) in the active label set is a function only of \(c_i=c|_{C_i}\), so one may compile each distinct pair \((a\to i,c_i)\) exactly once.

More explicitly, for complete parent assignments \(s,s'\in\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\), the compiled relation activated at \(C_i=c_i\) is
\[
s|_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\setminus\{a\}}
=s'|_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\setminus\{a\}},
\qquad
s|_{C_i}=s'|_{C_i}=c_i
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\theta_i(\,\cdot\mid s)=\theta_i(\,\cdot\mid s').
\tag{1}
\]
The label semantics say precisely that, in context \(c\), the complete primitive mechanism of \(i\) does not depend on parent \(a\). Such mechanism invariance implies (1) after taking the distribution of the mechanism's independent response noise. Conversely, order the finite states of \(i\), introduce an independent \(E_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\), and represent a CPT by
\[
f_i(s,E_i):=\min\left\{z:\sum_{z'\le z}\theta_i(z'\mid s)\ge E_i\right\}.
\]
If (1) holds, the cumulative sums, and hence \(f_i(s,e)\), are identical for all \(e\in(0,1)\) when only \(s_a\) changes in the active context. Thus the CPT has a label-compatible structural representation without changing any observational or interventional distribution. Therefore, in the stochastic-CPT representation, a table satisfies all compiled whole-row relations if and only if it is compatible with every label in \(L_{C_0}\). By \(\texttt{def:observed-csi-model-class}\), membership in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0}))\) additionally imposes exactly the fixed finite state spaces, latent-root restriction, two-child-latent restriction, independent latent roots, and strict primitive positivity collected in \(\Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G)\). Therefore, in both directions,
\[
\theta\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}\!\left(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\right)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\theta\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0})
\text{ and }
\theta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G),
\]
which proves the asserted class equality and verifies the second line of the replacement construction directly from the first. Notice that this is an intersection with the published class, not a replacement of that class by a new one.

We next compare the finite graphical syntax. For \(c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}\), let \(k(c)\) denote the fiber of the compiled joint activation truth-table map that contains assignments with control value \(c\). This is well defined even if two full control assignments lie in the same fiber: maximality then gives the same active labels. Let \(t_c\) enumerate once each edge having a compiled relation active on \(k(c)\). The preceding equivalence gives
\[
\{e:e\text{ occurs in }t_c\}=L_{C_0}(c).
\tag{2}
\]
Every entry is CSI-authorized on \(k(c)\), so \(t_c\) is an authorized trace. By \(\texttt{def:context-graph}\) and (2),
\[
H_{k(c),t_c}=G\setminus L_{C_0}(c).
\]
Removing the observed control roots therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_{k(c),t_c}[(V\setminus C_0)\cup U]
&=\Bigl((V\setminus C_0)\cup U,
      \bigl(E(G)\setminus L_{C_0}(c)\bigr)
      \cap(((V\setminus C_0)\cup U)\times((V\setminus C_0)\cup U))\Bigr)\\
&=\Bigl((V\setminus C_0)\cup U,
      \bigl(E(G)\cap(((V\setminus C_0)\cup U)\times((V\setminus C_0)\cup U))\bigr)
      \setminus L_{C_0}(c)\Bigr)\\
&=G_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the context graphs are identical, not merely Markov equivalent.

For the row quotient, define a finite undirected graph \(B_i^L\) whose vertices are the complete assignments in \(\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\), with an edge between \(s\) and \(s'\) exactly when (1) is one of the equalities generated by a label. By construction of \(\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\), its primitive row-equality graph for child \(i\) is literally \(B_i^L\). By \(\texttt{def:row-quotient}\),
\[
\mathcal R_i=\pi_0(B_i^L),
\tag{4}
\]
the set of connected components. Equation (4) is the connected equality closure of the published labels, and \(\texttt{thm:canonical-row-quotient}\) ensures that passing to this quotient changes neither the compatible table class nor its observed or interventional maps.

It remains to compare returned formulas and to separate that comparison from a converse claim. Fix
\(
\theta\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0})).
\)
Strict primitive positivity and finiteness imply, for every complete observed assignment \(v\),
\[
P_\theta(V=v)
=\sum_{u\in\mathcal X_U}
  \prod_{j\in V\cup U}
  \theta_j\!\left((v,u)_j\mid(v,u)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(j)}\right)>0.
\tag{5}
\]
The sum is finite and nonempty, and each summand is a product of strictly positive coordinates. Summing (5) over assignments extending \(C_0=c\) gives
\[
P_\theta(C_0=c)>0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus every conditional observed law \(P_\theta(V\setminus C_0\mid C_0=c)\) is defined by a divisor certified positive on the model class.

Because every member of \(C_0\) is a root and \(X\cap C_0=\varnothing\), truncated factorization gives
\[
P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(C_0=c)=P_\theta(C_0=c).
\tag{7}
\]
Conditioning that same factorization on \(C_0=c\) fixes the root mechanisms and deletes the label-active edges. In view of (3), the resulting postintervention law is the context-model law on \(G_c\), and hence
\[
P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y\mid C_0=c)
=P^{(c)}_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y).
\tag{8}
\]
Suppose ordinary identification in every \(G_c\) returns \(F_c\). The cited Shpitser--Pearl output theorem and (8) give
\[
F_c\!\left(P_\theta(V\setminus C_0\mid C_0=c)\right)
=P^{(c)}_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)
=P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y\mid C_0=c).
\tag{9}
\]
Starting from observed cells, the conditioning in (9) uses the positive denominator (6); the remaining marginalization, conditioning, district restriction, and leaf-removal nodes of the ordinary derivation are constructors allowed by \(\texttt{def:success-derivation}\), and every edge deletion is justified by \(t_c\). Therefore these are compiled SUCCESS derivations. Total probability, followed by (7) and (9), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)
&=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}}
  P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(\mathbf y\mid C_0=c)
  P_{\theta,\mathbf x}(C_0=c)\\
&=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_{C_0}}
  P_\theta(C_0=c)
  F_c\!\left(P_\theta(V\setminus C_0\mid C_0=c)\right)\\
&=E(P_\theta(V)).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
The sum is finite, and all divisors have recorded positivity judgments, so \(E\in\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). This is exactly the assembly in the cited Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash algorithm. Its validity on this note's class also follows from \(\texttt{thm:success-soundness}\).

The logical direction transferred in (10) is the correct one. The class equality gives
\[
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}\!\left(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\right)
\subseteq \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0}).
\tag{11}
\]
An observed-law functional valid on the right side of (11) remains valid on the left side. By contrast, a pair witnessing nonidentification on the right need not have the fixed latent cardinalities or strictly positive primitive CPT coordinates required on the left. Thus the published necessity proof does not, merely by restriction, supply a countermodel pair in this note's class. No converse for the intersection is used or claimed.

Finally, in \(\mathsf E_5\) the activation predicate is \(X=0\), the activated whole-row relation is
\[
P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=0)=\frac12
=P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=1),
\]
with the complementary \(Z=1\) probabilities equal as well. Hence it is a whole-row CSI with an observed activation variable, as required by \(\texttt{ass:observed-activation}\) and \(\texttt{ass:whole-row-csi}\). But the displayed graph contains \(U\to X\), so \(X\) is not a root. Indeed, every observed vertex of \(\mathsf E_5\) has a parent: \(U\to X\), \(T\to Z\) and \(X\to Z\), and \(U,T,Z\to Y\). Therefore its nonconstant activation cannot be represented by a control set contained in the observed roots. This proves strict enlargement of the permitted input syntax beyond observed-root controls.

The resulting procedure must be sound and complete. On maximal-regular observed-root inputs, the required comparison is the compilation proved in \(\texttt{thm:root-control-class-bridge}\): identical connected row quotients and context graphs, together with agreement with the Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash returned formula whenever their per-context identification criterion succeeds. A semantic nonidentification converse on this note's narrower fixed-cardinality, strictly primitive-positive class is required only if supported by a separate countermodel construction in that class. proposed.name: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)\)
proposed.construction:
The definition has the following extensionally equivalent two-line form. First,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)
:=\{\vartheta\in\Theta(G):{}&\text{ every latent vertex is a parentless root with exactly two observed children,}\\
&\text{the latent roots are mutually independent, every primitive CPT entry is strictly positive,}\\
&\text{every activation variable in }\mathcal C\text{ is observed, and every whole-row equality in }\mathcal C\text{ holds}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Second, let \((G,L_{C_0})\) be a maximal-regular labeled-DAG input whose controls \(C_0\subseteq V\) are observed roots, and let \(\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\) be the whole-row compilation that, whenever \(a\to i\in L_{C_0}(c)\), equates the complete conditional vectors of child \(i\) across values of parent \(a\) under the activation \(C_i=c|_{C_i}\), where \(C_i=\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\cap C_0\). Put \(\mathbf d=(|\mathcal X_j|:j\in V\cup U)\), write \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0})\) for the published compatible labeled-DAG CPT class, and define
\[
\Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G)
:=\{\vartheta\in\Theta(G):\text{the fixed finite state spaces, latent-root, two-child-latent, independent-latent, and strict primitive-positivity restrictions hold}\}.
\]
On this compiled input, the same set is
\[
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}\!\left(G,\mathcal C(L_{C_0})\right)
=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{MJEK}}(G,L_{C_0})\cap\Theta^{\mathrm{sm},+}_{\mathbf d}(G).
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the required semantically unchanged rewrite: the first line spells out the existing finite strictly positive semi-Markovian whole-row-CSI class, and the second records its exact specialization on compiled maximal-regular observed-root inputs as the published compatible class intersected with the already imposed fixed finite-state, semi-Markovian, and strict primitive-positivity restrictions.

proposed.justification: This is the unresolved completeness kernel: multi-district local failures must glue through shared rows into a genuine global query-changing direction or force total arithmetic recovery. proposed.gap: Tikka et al. leave general CSI completeness unresolved; the Mokhtarian et al. theorem applies to maximal-regular observed-root controls and transfers automatically only in its success direction to this note's stricter fixed-cardinality positive class; Chen and Darwiche provide no complete state-specific obstruction theorem.
proposed.consumer: A positive answer is the missing mathematical basis for a total explanatory CSI-identification backend in \(Y_0\); the root-control bridge already supplies an exact successful-formula regression path.

obligation.what_is_open: A finite global theorem connecting exhaustive context-compatible factor failure to jointly quotient-supported, multi-block rooted-forest perturbations with zero full observed increment and nonzero full-query increment, together with total arithmetic recovery in every remaining case.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives provide neither a complete normal form for cross-context recovery nor a gluing theorem. A local C-forest does not imply a global direction after quotient row sharing, as the reference-context bow proves; conversely, exhausting an active deletion can erase the only usable forest, as the five-node example proves. The root-control bridge settles syntax and successful-formula agreement but supplies no multi-block countermodel in the endogenous-activation class. Generic real-algebraic feasibility would decide semantic fibers but would not establish the required forest linkage or descent to the permitted arithmetic-expression class.
obligation.attempted: The proof was reduced first to retained partial traces and then to row-space tests on residual forest-supported blocks. The one-block fixed-nuisance sink case closes exactly. Blockwise nullspace intersection still fails without controlling changes in nuisance tables and cross-district cancellation. Separately, maximal-regular observed-root inputs were compiled exactly and their successful formulas were shown to agree, isolating rather than solving the remaining global gluing step.
obligation.partial_result: The exact row quotient, sound SUCCESS assembly, fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine reduction, corrected row-space/nullspace alternative, and positive two-model certificate are proved. The forest-to-kernel lift yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported rational null vector. The five-node example proves that maximal active deletion can erase the obstruction, while the bow example proves that a local forest can be annihilated by a shared observed reference context. The root-control bridge proves exact compilation of maximal-regular observed-root inputs, equality with the published class intersected with this note's fixed finite strictly primitive-positive CPT class, identical context graphs and row quotient, and agreement of successful returned formulas; it deliberately transfers no nonidentification converse to that intersection. Thus the remaining theorem must retain partial traces and solve a jointly shared-row multi-block contraction problem whose separating direction changes the full query.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved root-control bridge into the narrowed comparator clause and synchronize the open-obligation metadata.

proposed.comparator_claim: Corollary 2 states completeness of ordinary identification, with failure yielding a hedge through Theorem 6.
Theorem 5 proves termination and soundness of CSI search, while Theorem 6 shows that separate identification in every context graph is not complete.

Theorem 1 is an if-and-only-if criterion for the labeled-DAG class with observed-root controls, treatment and outcome outside the controls, and maximal-regular labels; Algorithm 1 assembles the successful per-context formulas.
Theorem 1 proves soundness of a returned state-specific formula, and the paper does not claim general CSI completeness.
Theorem 1 characterizes classical positive-model identification through an invariant arithmetic-circuit cut found by the c-component method.
Theorem 1 states that the polynomial program gives sharp bounds for the encoded finite discrete causal problem.
The paper characterizes observational and interventional equivalence for fully observed context-specific staged-tree representations.
Theorem 4 gives a sound-and-complete procedure for conditional generalized identification under positivity.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Mokhtarian comparator is now matched by an exact syntactic and successful-formula bridge, while its semantic converse is not promised on the narrower fixed-cardinality positive class.

open_obligations.obstruction: The primitives still provide neither a complete cross-context recovery normal form nor a gluing theorem. The forest-to-kernel lift yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported rational null vector. The five-node example proves that maximal active deletion can erase the obstruction, while the bow example proves that a local forest can be annihilated by a shared observed reference context. The root-control bridge proves exact compilation of maximal-regular observed-root inputs, equality with the published class intersected with this note's fixed finite strictly primitive-positive CPT class, identical context graphs and row quotient, and agreement of successful returned formulas; it deliberately transfers no nonidentification converse to that intersection. Thus the remaining theorem must retain partial traces and solve a jointly shared-row multi-block contraction problem whose separating direction changes the full query.

prose_updates.tldr: Fixed treatment and outcome assignments activate observed CSI information that variable-level identification can discard, but a local forest alone need not survive shared rows across contexts. In the settled fixed-nuisance binary-sink base case, the proved forest-to-kernel lift yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported rational null vector, and a positive baseline plus an explicit radius yields two global quotient-shared models with the same observed law and different queries. A new root-control bridge compiles maximal-regular observed-root labels into identical context graphs and row quotients and reproduces every successful published formula on the published class intersected with this note's fixed finite, strictly primitive-positive CPT class. The multi-block global dichotomy remains open and must be settled before any complete procedure is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Tikka et al. give sound CSI calculus and show that separate context graphs are incomplete. Mokhtarian et al. prove an if-and-only-if theorem for maximal-regular observed-root controls, but after intersection with this note's fixed-cardinality strictly primitive-positive CPT class only their successful identification formula transfers automatically. Chen and Darwiche give sound state-specific procedures without a complete obstruction theorem, and a local forest can be neutralized by cross-context row sharing.
project_justification.fill: The project certifies the exact binary-sink lift through a forest-restricted row-space alternative and baseline perturbation, proves an exact syntactic and successful-formula bridge for maximal-regular observed-root inputs, and leaves the provenance-carrying multi-block context-factor dichotomy visibly open.

prose_updates.related_work: Boutilier et al. define local CSI through equality of conditional behavior, and Pensar et al. encode such equalities by labels; these works inform the canonical quotient. Shpitser and Pearl establish ordinary formula-or-hedge completeness, recovered when the CSI list is empty. Tikka et al., Theorems 5--6, prove sound CSI search and show that separate context-graph identification is insufficient; the open global dichotomy would add necessity. Mokhtarian et al., Theorem 1, prove an if-and-only-if criterion for their labeled-DAG class under its maximal-regularity hypotheses, with control variables restricted to observed roots and treatment and outcome outside the controls. The root-control bridge proves identical compiled context graphs and row quotient and agreement of successful returned formulas. Because this note additionally fixes finite cardinalities and requires strictly positive primitive CPTs, the compiled class is the published class intersected with that stricter CPT class; only the published identification implication transfers automatically, not its nonidentification converse. Chen and Darwiche supply sound state-specific procedures and an active-pruning warning but no general completeness theorem. Their circuit work and Duarte et al.'s sharp polynomial programs inform finite algebraic contraction but do not provide a forest-derived shared-row kernel. Kivva et al. supply a positivity-aware generalized-identification comparator. Duarte and Solus characterize fully observed context-specific representations rather than latent query fibers. Bhattacharya et al. provide downstream estimation after a functional is returned, and the \(Y_0\) paper supplies the direct software consumer.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The canonical quotient, SUCCESS soundness, fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine map, forest-to-kernel row-space alternative, baseline perturbation soundness theorem, finite structural bound, two rational boundary fixtures, and root-control class bridge are supporting results. The bridge gives identical syntax and successful-formula agreement on maximal-regular observed-root inputs; it does not transfer the published nonidentification converse to this note's narrower fixed-cardinality positive intersection. The global context-factor dichotomy is visibly open and remains the completeness kernel. No general certificate-soundness or complete procedure is claimed before multi-block forest lifting is established. Strict primitive-CPT positivity and observed endogenous activation are transparent scope conditions. Estimation is downstream.

proofs.proof_tex:
We first verify the five-node pair directly from \(\texttt{def:five-node-rational-instance}\).  Write
\[
 a_u=P(X=0\mid U=u),\qquad (a_0,a_1)=\left(\frac34,\frac14\right).
\]
The latent roots \(U\) and \(T\) are independent and fair.  The equality
\[
 P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=0)=P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=1)=\frac12
\]
is exactly the asserted whole-row CSI; complementation gives the same equality for \(Z=1\).  Its activation variable \(X\) is observed, but the arrow \(U\to X\) makes \(X\) a nonroot.  Thus this input explicitly witnesses the permitted endogenous observed-activation syntax and is not an input whose activation variable is required to be an observed root.

For either \(z\in\{0,1\}\), finite marginalization and the preceding CSI give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X=0,Z=z)
 &=\sum_{u,t}P(U=u)P(T=t)P(X=0\mid U=u)P(Z=z\mid X=0,T=t)\\
 &=\sum_{u,t}\frac14 a_u\frac12
 =\frac14.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Put \(s_t=P(Z=0\mid X=1,T=t)\), so \((s_0,s_1)=(3/4,1/4)\).  Independence of \(U\) and \(T\) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X=1,Z=0)
 &=\frac14\sum_{u,t}(1-a_u)s_t
 =\frac14\left(\sum_u(1-a_u)\right)\left(\sum_t s_t\right)
 =\frac14,\\
 P(X=1,Z=1)
 &=\frac14\left(\sum_u(1-a_u)\right)\left(\sum_t(1-s_t)\right)
 =\frac14.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Hence \((X,Z)\) is uniform under both displayed models.  Every outcome row of \(\rho^+_5\) is \(1/2\), so
\[
 P_{\rho^+_5}(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=\frac14\frac12=\frac18
 \quad\text{for all }x,z,y\in\{0,1\}.
\]

Only the four \(Z=0\) probabilities of \(Y=1\) change in \(\rho^-_5\).  In the order \((U,T)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), let
\[
 \Delta=\left(\frac3{100},\frac3{100},\frac7{100},-\frac{25}{100}\right)
\]
be the vector \(P_{\rho^-_5}(Y=1\mid U,T,Z=0)-P_{\rho^+_5}(Y=1\mid U,T,Z=0)\).  For \((X,Z)=(0,0)\), the four unnormalized latent weights are
\[
 \left(P(U=u,T=t,X=0,Z=0)\right)_{u,t}
 =\frac1{32}(3,3,1,1).
\]
Therefore the increment of the corresponding observed \(Y=1\) cell is
\[
 \frac1{32}(3,3,1,1)\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac{9+9+7-25}{3200}=0.
\]
For \((X,Z)=(1,0)\), the four weights are
\[
 \left(P(U=u,T=t,X=1,Z=0)\right)_{u,t}
 =\frac1{64}(3,1,9,3),
\]
and the observed-cell increment is
\[
 \frac1{64}(3,1,9,3)\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac{9+3+63-75}{6400}=0.
\]
The outcome rows at \(Z=1\) are unchanged.  Thus every observed \(Y=1\) cell agrees.  Since the \((X,Z)\)-marginals also agree and each binary outcome row is normalized, every observed \(Y=0\) cell agrees as well.  Consequently all eight cells under \(\rho^-_5\) also equal \(1/8\).

Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), intervention replaces only the mechanism for \(X\); the two latent roots remain independent and fair, and the CSI row gives \(P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=t)=1/2\).  The change in the interventional cell is therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{X=0}^{\rho^-_5}(Y=1)-P_{X=0}^{\rho^+_5}(Y=1)
 &=\sum_{u,t}P(U=u)P(T=t)P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=t)\Delta_{ut}\\
 &=\frac18\left(\frac{3+3+7-25}{100}\right)
 =-\frac3{200}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first query equals \(1/2\), because all of its outcome rows equal \(1/2\).  Hence
\[
 P_{X=0}^{\rho^+_5}(Y=1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 P_{X=0}^{\rho^-_5}(Y=1)=\frac12-\frac3{200}=\frac{97}{200}.
\]
Every displayed primitive probability and every binary complement lies strictly between zero and one; all tables are normalized, the roots are independent, and each latent root has exactly the two children displayed in the definition.  Thus the calculation uses two positive semi-Markovian models satisfying the input CSI, and their query gap is exactly \(3/200\).

We next verify the trace assertions.  In the treatment state \(X=0\), the CSI authorizes deletion of \(T\to Z\).  After this deletion, latent projection has directed edges \(X\to Z\to Y\) and the single bidirected edge \(X\leftrightarrow Y\): the edge \(Z\leftrightarrow Y\) induced by the common latent parent \(T\) disappears when \(T\to Z\) is deleted.  Consider any pair satisfying \(\texttt{def:rooted-forest-obstruction}\) in this pruned graph.  Its larger forest must meet the treatment set.  If its vertex set is \(\{X\}\), its childless set contains \(X\), which is not a vertex of \(\operatorname{An}_{H\setminus X}(Y)\).  If it also contains \(Y\), bidirected connectedness forces its bidirected component to be contained in \(\{X,Y\}\); it cannot contain \(Z\), because \(Z\) is incident to no bidirected edge.  But the induced subgraph on \(\{X,Y\}\) has no directed edge, so its childless set is \(\{X,Y\}\), again not contained in \(\operatorname{An}_{H\setminus X}(Y)\).  These exhaust the bidirected-connected possibilities meeting \(X\).  Hence the pruned graph has no rooted C-forest pair of the required kind.

For the empty trace in the original latent projection, use the activation-refining cell \(Z=0\) and take
\[
 F=\{Y\},\qquad F'=\{X,Z,Y\}.
\]
The bidirected edges \(X\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(Z\leftrightarrow Y\) make \(F'\) one district.  The directed forest edges \(X\to Z\to Y\) give each vertex at most one directed child, and both \(F\) and \(F'\) have the common childless set \(R_0=\{Y\}\).  Moreover,
\[
 F\cap X=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 F'\cap X\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 R_0\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G\setminus X}(Y).
\]
Thus this is a rooted C-forest pair under \(\texttt{def:rooted-forest-obstruction}\).

Regard \(\Delta\) as a perturbation of the four outcome-row classes with \(Z=0\), and extend it by zero on every outcome-row class with \(Z=1\).  It is then supported on the row classes exposed by the displayed \(Z=0\) forest.  The two observed \(Y=1\) increments computed above are the only potentially nonzero observed increments.  They vanish; the \(Z=1\) increments vanish by the zero extension, and the corresponding \(Y=0\) increments are their negatives by normalization.  By the contraction identity in \(\texttt{thm:fixed-sink-affine-map}\), equivalently by the defining contraction in \(\texttt{def:fixed-sink-linearization}\), this proves
\[
 A_{\eta,t,F}\Delta=0.
\]
The intervention calculation gives
\[
 b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\Delta=-\frac3{200}\ne0.
\]
Thus the displayed outcome-row difference lies in the relevant observed kernel while changing the query, as claimed.

Finally consider \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{bow}}\).  By \(\texttt{def:reference-context-bow-instance}\), \(A\) and \(U\) are independent and fair, and the \(A=0\) CSI gives
\[
 P(X=x\mid A=0,U=0)=P(X=x\mid A=0,U=1)=\frac12
 \quad (x\in\{0,1\}).
\]
The conditioning event has probability
\[
 P(A=0,X=x)=\sum_u\frac12\frac12\frac12=\frac14>0.
\]
Bayes' rule therefore gives \(P(U=u\mid A=0,X=x)=1/2\).  Intervention on \(X\) leaves the fair latent root \(U\) unchanged, and \(Y\) has no parent \(A\).  Using the four outcome rows from the definition,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{X=0}(Y=1)&=\frac12\left(\frac15+\frac35\right)=\frac25,\\
 P_{X=1}(Y=1)&=\frac12\left(\frac25+\frac45\right)=\frac35.
 \end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, for either \(x\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(A=0,X=x,Y=1)
 &=\sum_u P(A=0)P(U=u)P(X=x\mid A=0,U=u)P(Y=1\mid X=x,U=u)\\
 &=\frac18\sum_u P(Y=1\mid X=x,U=u)
 =\frac14 P_{X=x}(Y=1).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently
\[
 P_{X=0}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=0,Y=1)=\frac25,
 \qquad
 P_{X=1}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=1,Y=1)=\frac35,
\]
in agreement with the displayed observed cells \(1/10\) and \(3/20\).

For the structural rejection, order the outcome-row coordinates as
\[
 (p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})
 =\bigl(P(Y=1\mid X=x,U=u): (x,u)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\bigr).
\]
The two intervention coefficient vectors are
\[
 b_0^{\mathsf T}=\left(\frac12,\frac12,0,0\right),
 \qquad
 b_1^{\mathsf T}=\left(0,0,\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
The rows of the full observed-cell coefficient matrix belonging to \((A,X,Y)=(0,0,1)\) and \((0,1,1)\) are, respectively,
\[
 \left(\frac18,\frac18,0,0\right)=\frac14 b_0^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \left(0,0,\frac18,\frac18\right)=\frac14 b_1^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus both query vectors belong to the row space of the full observed-cell matrix.  The same equality remains true after applying the common forest-support column restriction prescribed by \(\texttt{def:fixed-sink-linearization}\).  Therefore the applicable vector \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\) lies in \(\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\).  The row-space alternative of \(\texttt{lem:forest-to-kernel-lift}\), together with the rejection rule in \(\texttt{def:binary-sink-verifier}\), makes \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}\) reject the local \(A=1\) bow forest before a kernel direction or a countermodel pair is formed.
